rgb.source_file_note: en_refine.json is RGB's own refined/recommended variant (fixed incorrect positive/negative documents and corrected some answers vs. en.json), per the RGB repository's README.
rgb.used_for_note: RGB's own evaluation harness derives BOTH 'negative rejection' (-> our retrieval_blindness) and 'noise robustness' (-> our retrieval_noise) tasks from this SAME file, distinguished only by which of positive/negative passages are included in the corpus (RGB's noise_rate parameter). We reproduce that same distinction at the loader level rather than using separate files.

lost_in_the_middle.license: see repository LICENSE file (copied to data/raw/lost_in_the_middle/LICENSE)
lost_in_the_middle.source_file_note: Used the '10_total_documents, gold_at_4' bucket only (1 gold + 9 distractor/padding passages per question) out of the repo's several available buckets (gold_at_0/4/9, 10/20/30-document variants, oracle) — our own condition-builder logic (conditions/builders.py) re-derives which documents are used and where gold is placed, so the position label baked into a specific file's native ctxs ordering is not load-bearing; any of the three gold_at_* files for the 10-document bucket yields the identical underlying document set.

sampling_method.description: Each failure mode's 30-item sample is drawn independently with random.Random(f'{seed}-{failure_mode_key}').sample(valid_items, n_questions) over that dataset's full pool of valid items (RGB: 300 items shared by both retrieval_blindness and retrieval_noise, drawn as two independent 30-item samples from the same pool; Lost in the Middle: 2655 items for evidence_ignorance). Per-item gold-passage selection among an item's multiple eligible positives (RGB only) additionally uses a per-item seeded RNG (f'{seed}-{failure_mode}-{item_id}-goldpick') rather than always taking the first listed positive.

rgb: positive (gold-supporting passages) list must be non-empty
negative (background/distractor passages) list must be non-empty
answer field must contain at least one non-empty answer string
lost_in_the_middle: answers list must contain at least one non-empty string
ctxs must contain exactly one entry with isgold=true
ctxs must contain at least 2 entries total (gold + >=1 distractor/padding)

exclusions.rgb: 0 of 300 en_refine.json records were excluded by the rules above — every record has a non-empty query, >=5 positive, >=5 negative, and >=1 non-empty answer string (verified directly against the downloaded file).
exclusions.lost_in_the_middle: 0 of 2655 records in the gold_at_4/10_total_documents file were excluded by the rules above — every record has exactly one isgold=true ctx and a non-empty answers list (verified directly against the downloaded file).

known_limitations: RGB and Lost in the Middle are both English-language, Wikipedia/news-centric public benchmarks, not an enterprise-style corpus — results characterize failure-mode behavior on these specific public distributions, not any particular production RAG system.

Lost in the Middle's reference_answer uses only answers[0] (the first of possibly several acceptable answer strings) for exact-match/F1 scoring — a documented simplification, not a defect in the source data.

RGB's retrieval_blindness and retrieval_noise samples are drawn independently from the same 300-item pool (not guaranteed disjoint) — a deliberate, documented design choice, since the two failure modes are analyzed separately and never compared item-for-item.
